sections.label: GST on imported services
sections.summary: MOF incorporated feedback into the Bill, ensuring the GST regime stays fair and resilient in a digital economy from 1 January 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) has evaluated all the feedback received and incorporated them where relevant to the draft text of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This measure will ensure that our GST regime remains fair and resilient in a digital economy and will take effect from 1 January 2020.

sections.label: Reverse charge and overseas vendor registration
sections.summary: GST on imported services will be introduced via a Reverse Charge mechanism for B2B services and an Overseas Vendor Registration regime for B2C services.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This means that GST ought to apply on local consumption of services, irrespective of whether the service is supplied in Singapore or from abroad.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, GST on imported services will be introduced through a Reverse Charge mechanism for business-to-business (B2B) imported services, and an Overseas Vendor Registration regime for business-to-consumer (B2C) imported services.

sections.label: Overseas Vendor Registration thresholds
sections.summary: Overseas suppliers and electronic marketplace operators must register for GST if they have global annual turnover of $1 million or more and sell at least $100,000 of digital services to local consumers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: On the B2C front, overseas suppliers and electronic marketplace operators will be required to register for GST under our Overseas Vendor Registration (OVR) regime, and they will have to register if they have a global annual turnover of $1 million or more and make sales of digital services of at least $100,000 to local consumers.

sections.label: Bill clauses on imported services
sections.summary: Clauses 5-20, 22-29 and 35-41 of the Bill provide for introducing GST on imported services with effect from 1 January 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Clauses 5-20, 22-29 and 35-41 of the Bill provide for the tax change that I just described on introducing GST on imported services, with effect from 1 January 2020.

sections.label: IRAS investigative powers
sections.summary: The amendments give authorised IRAS officers powers of forced entry, arrest without warrant and body search, subject to conditions, similar to UK and US tax authorities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments will enhance IRAS' investigative powers by providing authorised IRAS officers with the power of forced entry, the power to arrest without warrant, and the power to carry out body search, subject to conditions, and I should highlight that investigation officers of other tax authorities, such as the UK and US have similar powers to facilitate their investigations.

sections.label: Offences for unauthorised GST collection
sections.summary: The amendment makes unauthorised GST collection an offence, adds a custodial sentence, and creates a new offence for collecting more GST than allowed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To further protect consumers and strengthen deterrence against unauthorised collection of GST, the proposed amendment makes unauthorised collection of GST an offence, without reference to the issue of an invoice or a receipt for such collection.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The amendment also introduces a heavier punishment, by way of a custodial sentence, in cases where the offence is committed without reasonable excuse or through negligence.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In addition, our proposed amendment will counter unauthorised GST collection by introducing a new offence where a GST-registered person, or a person authorised to collect GST, collects more GST than what is allowed under the GST Act, without reasonable excuse or through negligence.

sections.label: GST increment and collection
sections.summary: Following the Budget 2018 announcement of a GST increase from 7% to 9%, there has been interest and suggestions on making GST collection more robust and equitable.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Following the Budget 2018 announcement on the imminent GST increment from the current 7% to 9%, there has been some interest and suggestions on what more MOF can do to make GST collection more robust and equitable.

sections.label: GST on imported products and services
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarifications on GST for imported products and services and supports changes to impose GST on them for B2B and B2C transactions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: First, I would like to seek clarifications on the GST imposed on imported products and services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am supportive of the changes to impose GST on imported products and services for both B2B and B2C transactions.

sections.label: Differential GST rates for luxury items
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to consider differential and higher GST rates for luxury items and certain items affecting social behaviour, giving examples.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Next, while this round of amendments does not involve differential GST rates, I would like to urge the Ministry to seriously consider imposing differential and higher GST rates, specifically for luxury items and certain other items that can have an impact on social behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To elaborate, luxury items would include more expensive alcoholic beverages, such as wine that cost more than $1,000 a bottle, and also luxury cars that cost more than $160,000 each, for instance.

sections.label: E-commerce industry revenue estimates
sections.summary: Estimates state the e-commerce industry will generate over US$3.7 billion in revenue in 2018 and grow to US$5.4 billion by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: According to some estimates, our e-commerce industry will generate over US$3.7 billion in revenue in 2018 alone, and the market is expected to grow to US$5.4 billion by the year 2025.

sections.label: GST on intangible media advertising
sections.summary: Subsection 2(a)(xi) extends GST to advertising services on intangible media platforms where the Comptroller is satisfied the advertisement is substantially promulgated in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Subsection 2(a)(xi) extends the GST to any advertising service on any intangible media platform, where the Comptroller is satisfied that the advertisement is intended to be substantially promulgated in Singapore.

sections.label: Taxing electronic marketplace operators
sections.summary: The Bill proposes to tax operators of electronic marketplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Bill also proposes to tax operators of electronic marketplaces.

sections.label: GST on online goods
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked whether it plans to extend GST to goods purchased online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Does the Ministry have plans to extend the GST to goods purchased online?

sections.label: Global mobile app market
sections.summary: The global mobile app market is estimated at US$77 billion in 2017 and US$200 billion in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For just mobile apps alone, the market is estimated to be US$77 billion globally in 2017 and poised to grow to US$200 billion in 2020.

sections.label: OVR revenue thresholds
sections.summary: The OVR threshold is $1 million global revenues and $100,000 Singapore revenues, with the global threshold called very low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The threshold for OVR is $1 million of global revenues and $100,000 of Singapore revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The $1 million global revenue threshold is very low.

sections.label: Expected tax revenue
sections.summary: The Government is asked how much revenue it expects to raise through this tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How much revenue does the Government expect to raise through this tax?

sections.label: Digital GST rebates proposal
sections.summary: GST on imported digital services could reduce consumption and price children out, so digital GST rebates are proposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The imposition of GST on such imported digital services could reduce their consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It could price children from lower-income families out of digital experiences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider some form of digital GST rebates, particularly for "virtuous" digital services, such as online learning and online education?

sections.label: SMEs and global tax trends
sections.summary: An SME desire for a level playing field is cited, and MOF is asked to comment on global tax trends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: What I heard from some SMEs is the desire for a level playing field, including on the issue of tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that today we are amending the GST to include online services for taxation purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can MOF comment on the global tax trends in both taxation of online service as well as online commerce of physical goods so that we can have a more informed debate?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my queries, I support the amendment Bill.

sections.label: Stakeholder feedback and implementation engagement
sections.summary: The speaker thanks stakeholders for feedback and says businesses will continue to be engaged ahead of implementation from 1 January 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Here, I would like to thank all stakeholders for providing us with feedback.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will continue to engage businesses as we prepare for implementation from 1 January 2020.

sections.label: Global turnover and local sales thresholds
sections.summary: The $1 million global turnover matches the GST registration threshold for local suppliers, while the $100,000 sales threshold covers overseas vendors with significant Singapore consumer sales.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The $1 million global turnover maintains parity with the GST registration threshold of local suppliers, while the $100,000 threshold on sales to Singapore ensures that we bring into the tax net overseas vendors with significant sales to consumers here.

sections.label: Heavier punishments for GST collection offences
sections.summary: The Bill proposes heavier punishments, including custodial sentence and new offences, to strengthen prosecution and deterrence of unauthorised GST collection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In this Bill, we have proposed heavier punishments, including custodial sentence and new offences to further strengthen prosecution and deterence of unauthorised collection of GST.

sections.label: GST on imported services revenue estimate
sections.summary: The Government will engage industry to keep GST for imported services effective, easy to comply and certain, expecting about $90 million additional revenue yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the Government's part, we will continue to engage the industry to keep the GST for imported services effective, easy to comply and certain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Mr Ong Teng Koon asked how much revenue will we expect to collect from GST on imported services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We expect additional revenue of about $90 million per year.

sections.label: GST on B2C digital services
sections.summary: B2C consultancy or advisory services are subject to GST if they meet the definition of digital services supplied over the Internet with minimal or no human intervention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For B2C consultancy or advisory services, they will be subject to GST if the services meet the definition of "digital services", that is, if the service is supplied over the Internet or other electronic network with minimal or no human intervention.

sections.label: Singapore threshold stands at $400
sections.summary: The speaker states that in Singapore this threshold stands at $400.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In Singapore, I am sure Members are aware, this threshold stands at $400.

sections.label: Australia Vendor Collection GST
sections.summary: Australia is first to implement a Vendor Collection regime for overseas suppliers to collect GST on imported goods in July.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Australia is the first in the world to implement a Vendor Collection regime for overseas suppliers to collect GST on imported goods in July this year.

sections.label: Singapore broad-based single-rate GST
sections.summary: Singapore's broad-based single-rate GST with permanent GSTV is described as more equitable, progressive, with lower rates for lower-income and full rate for highest means.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In some jurisdictions, attempts at classification have resulted in bizarre outcomes, endless disputes and loopholes that may very well be exploited and end up being counter-productive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, Singapore’s adoption of a broad-based, single-rate GST regime, coupled with the permanent GSTV Scheme, is a more equitable approach in creating a fair and progressive tax system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have a broad-based single rate GST, but we couple that with a permanent GSTV which provides targeted transfers and help at the lower-income and retiree households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: By doing so, we create a GST system that is progressive, that effectively has lower tax rates for the lower-income while those with the highest means pay at the full rate.

sections.label: MOF reviews tax regime
sections.summary: Duties are reviewed regularly, and MOF will continue to review the tax regime for relevance and effectiveness in the digital economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And so, these duties are reviewed regularly and updated from time to time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I would thus like to reassure everyone that MOF will continue to review our tax regime regularly to ensure its relevance and effectiveness in the digital economy.
